record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Onset of asymptotic behavior of electromagnetic form factors
record.original_question: At what momentum-transfer scale do hadron or nucleon electromagnetic form factors reach their asymptotic regime, so that one can test both QCD-inspired asymptotic expectations and the analytic Phragmén-Lindelöf constraint that a form factor has the same limiting value in the space-like limit q^2 → -∞ and in the time-like limit q^2 → +∞?

evidence.quote: • when the asymptotic region is reached?
The Phr`agmen-Lindel¨of theorem [22] gives a rigorous prescription for the asymptotic behavior of analytical functions: limq2→−∞ F(SL)(q2) = limq2→∞ F(T L)(q2).
Therefore, the study of FFs at large Q2 represents a unique tool to understanding these properties of the nucleon electrodynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F(q^2) denote a hadron (in particular nucleon) electromagnetic form factor, regarded as an analytic function of the four-momentum transfer squared q^2 in the complex plane, with the space-like region corresponding to q^2 < 0 and the time-like region to q^2 > 0. The Phragmén–Lindelöf theorem, applied to such an analytic function, asserts that, provided F is bounded along suitable rays, its limiting values in the space-like and time-like asymptotic directions coincide:

   lim_{q^2 → -∞} F_{SL}(q^2) = lim_{q^2 → +∞} F_{TL}(q^2).

Perturbative QCD also predicts a definite asymptotic scaling behavior (for example, a Dirac form factor falling as 1/Q^4 up to logarithms, with the Pauli form factor suppressed by an additional 1/Q^2).

Problem. Determine the momentum-transfer scale Q^2 = |q^2| at which the electromagnetic form factors of hadrons, and of the nucleon in particular, actually enter their asymptotic regime, i.e. the scale above which both
  (a) the QCD-inspired asymptotic scaling predictions, and
  (b) the Phragmén–Lindelöf equality of the space-like and time-like limits
become quantitatively valid for the measured space-like and time-like form factors.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (dispersion-theoretical analyses, vector-meson-dominance fits, and time-like measurements such as those probing oscillating features of the nucleon form factors) continues to investigate the onset of asymptotic behavior and the Phragmén–Lindelöf equality between space-like and time-like limits. Current data show that even at the highest accessible Q^2 the predicted asymptotic regime has not been clearly reached, and the space-like and time-like form factors still differ markedly. The question of the precise scale of onset thus remains an open experimental and theoretical issue.

status_evidence.title: Dispersion-theoretical analysis of the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon
status_evidence.snippet: Phragmén–Lindelöf theorem extends space-like asymptotic behavior to the time-like region; asymptotic regime not yet established by data.
status_evidence.claim: Onset scale of asymptotic regime in nucleon form factors remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Understanding oscillating features of the time-like nucleon electromagnetic form factors
status_evidence.snippet: Time-like nucleon form factors exhibit oscillating, non-asymptotic features at currently measured Q^2.
status_evidence.claim: Time-like data show non-asymptotic behavior, indicating asymptotic regime not yet reached.

status_evidence.title: Timelike and spacelike electromagnetic form factors of nucleons, a unified description
status_evidence.snippet: Unified description still required; space-like and time-like form factors differ at accessible Q^2.
status_evidence.claim: Equality predicted by Phragmén–Lindelöf has not been verified experimentally.
